newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc will continue asset sales.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc will continue asset sales.

text.p: French chemicals and pharmaceutical group Rhone-Poulenc SA will continue its 10 billion french franc ($1.93 billion) asset sale programme, of which over half will be realised this year, and boost its profitability in the next few years, accordingto a press report published on Monday.
Jean-Rene Fourtou, chairman and chief executive, told La Tribune Desfosses newspaper that the company's board had decided against a demerger but would concentrate the company more on pharmaceuticals.

Fourtou said Rhone should have earnings per share growth -- before exceptionals -- of 20 percent in 1996, 1997 and 1998 and bring back its debt ratio to below 50 percent from 72 percent by the end of next year.
Fourtou also said that a takeover of Sanofi, the drugs unit of Elf Aquitaine, made no sense because it would not bring any synergies.
"In the U.S., investors look at profitability. If chemicals and fibres, once reorganised, have a rate of return on capital invested of more than 13 percent, our strategy makes sense," Fourtou said.
"The Americans have confidence in us. Since the start of the year it's them who are buying our shares. It is an American pension fund, Wellington, which is becoming our biggest shareholder," he said.
"If the supervisory board has not retained the option of a demerger, although it has been studied, it is because the board bets on a strong rise in the value of our shares," Fourtou said.
"For that we need a significant rise in our results. The group should increase its earnings per share (before exceptionals) by 20 percent per year in 1996, 1997 and 1998," he added.

"That also means a reduction in our debt level. We must, as planned, reduce the debt ratio to 50 percent from the end of next year after it had risen to 72 percent on the back of the Fisons acquisition," he said.
"How do we do that? By increasing our results and by a programme of asset sales of 10 billion francs, of which more than half will be completed by the end of the year," he said.
Fourtou said that while a demerger had been studied, Rhone-Poulenc's portfolio of activities was less dispersed than that of ICI before the demerger into ICIand Zeneca.
"The portfolio of Rhone-Poulenc, with two-thirds of activities in life sciences, is today close to the profile of Zeneca, which includes, like us, chemical specialties," he said.
"Indebted since the 1970s, Rhone-Poulenc has concentrated its activities by asset sales and has withdrawn from petrochemicals, PVC plastics, from TDI, acetic acid etc."
"The right formula, for us and our shareholders, is to continue that concentration, notably by asset sales, and improve our profitability," he said.
